title: The Quiet Vow
premise: Kestrel Galloway has built a career on other people's voices, ghostwriting a rival author's memoirs while nursing a decade-old heartbreak he's never spoken aloud. When his sister demands a plus-one for the Galloway family reunion, he hires Wren Ashby, a charming stranger, to play his boyfriend for one weekend. But the reunion forces Kestrel home to the coastal town where his first love, Theo, died in an accident Kestrel believes was his fault, and Wren's kindness cracks open the grief he's kept past tense. As the fake romance turns real, Kestrel learns Theo survived that night, alive but estranged, and is attending the same reunion. In the climax, Kestrel finally speaks the rehearsed sentence—an apology ten years overdue—and chooses to stop hiding behind borrowed words, ending with him claiming both love and his own name.
about_author: Edmund Ravensworth is the pen name of a former lighthouse keeper's assistant who spent fifteen years writing obituaries for a small coastal newspaper before turning to fiction. He writes romances about people who mistake silence for safety, drawing on the fog-bound towns of his childhood.

chapters.title: The Ghost in the Margins
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. We meet him mid-ghostwrite, erasing himself from a rival's memoir while dodging his sister Priya's reunion invitation. A chance encounter with Wren Ashby at a bookshop leads to a transactional arrangement: one weekend, one fake relationship. Emotional beat: loneliness disguised as professionalism; Kestrel believes invisibility is safety.

chapters.title: Saltwater Reckoning
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV, with Wren interludes. The reunion begins at the family's seaside inn, and every room holds a memory of Theo. Wren plays his role too well, and by dessert their staged intimacy feels dangerously real. Kestrel spots a familiar stranger across the lawn—Theo, alive. Emotional beat: dread colliding with unexpected tenderness.

chapters.title: What the Tide Returned
chapters.summary: Alternating POV between Kestrel and Theo. Confrontation on the bluffs: Theo reveals he survived, disfigured and bitter, believing Kestrel abandoned him deliberately. Kestrel's carefully constructed identity as 'the one who moved on' collapses. Meanwhile Wren, hurt by being a stand-in, gives Kestrel an ultimatum. Emotional beat: shattering—the price of survival exposed.

chapters.title: The Quiet Vow
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV, closing with Theo's. At the reunion's final bonfire, Kestrel publicly speaks the rehearsed sentence—his apology, his truth, his own name claimed as author of his life. He releases Theo with grace and chooses Wren, this time without a script. Emotional beat: resolution through voice; found family embraces him as he finally stops disappearing.
